[General] Setting the ThreadLocal to `NOP` here can silently corrupt outer state.

`beforeDefineClass` now returns `DefineClassContextImpl.NOP` for the J9ROMCLASSCOOKIE path **without** calling `enter()` (so the ThreadLocal is not pushed). But `afterDefineClass` has been simplified to always call `context.exit()`, so `NOP.exit()` runs — and since `NOP.previous` is `null`, this line writes `NOP` into `defineClassContext`.

In a nested scenario (outer `beforeDefineClass` triggers a nested class definition via `Class.forName` during super-type resolution, and the nested class hits the J9 path), the inner `NOP.exit()` overwrites the outer context with `NOP`. Between that point and the outer `afterDefineClass`, `isFailedClass()` / `getSuperTypes()` will read `NOP` instead of the outer context.

Consider making `exit()` a no-op on `NOP` (e.g. early-return when `this == NOP`), or restore the previous behavior of skipping `exit()` when `beforeDefineClass` returned the no-op sentinel.

replies.body: Rebased onto current `main` and addressed this in the refreshed branch. I kept the `null`/no-context behavior for the J9ROMCLASSCOOKIE and ignored-class-loader paths, and updated the nullability on `DefineClassHelper` / `DefineClassHandler` so the contract matches that behavior under NullAway. That avoids the outer-frame clobbering concern while preserving the existing semantics for the no-op path.

More explicitly: the refreshed branch does **not** use `NOP` as the returned no-op context for the J9 / ignored-class-loader paths anymore. `beforeDefineClass(...)` now returns `null` on those paths again, and `afterDefineClass(...)` null-checks before calling `exit()`. So in the scenario you described there is no inner `NOP.exit()` call at all, which is what avoids clobbering an outer active frame. `NOP` is only retained as the ThreadLocal's default / fallback sentinel for real entered contexts.

[General] Behavior change worth confirming: previously, in declarative-config mode, the returned `AutoConfiguredOpenTelemetrySdk.getConfig()` was `null`. Downstream callers (`AgentInstaller.setBootstrapPackages`, `configureIgnoredTypes`, `BeforeAgentListener#beforeAgent`, `AgentExtension#extend`) now receive an empty-map-backed `ConfigProperties` instead.

Any extension that disambiguated declarative mode via `config == null` will silently switch to the empty-config branch. Is this the intended contract going forward? If so, it's probably worth noting in the changelog / extension docs.

replies.body: Rebased onto current `main` and removed this behavior change from `OpenTelemetryInstaller` in the refreshed branch, so declarative-config mode is no longer normalized to empty config here. Separately, the broader extension-SPI direction ended up being handled in #19148, which introduced the no-config overloads / deprecation path instead.

The `instrumentation` local is only forwarded into the constructor, so it can be inlined.

```suggestion
    InstrumentationModuleInstaller instrumentationModuleInstaller =
        new InstrumentationModuleInstaller(InstrumentationHolder.getInstrumentation());
```

[Style] `requireNonNull` runs once per element in the stream; hoist it outside. Guard on `!helperClassNames.isEmpty()` to preserve the current semantics (no failure when the list is empty, as the message implies).

Something like:

```java
if (!helperClassNames.isEmpty()) {
  requireNonNull(
      helpersSource,
      "helpersSource must not be null when helperClassNames is non-empty");
}
List<HelperClassDefinition> helpers =
    helperClassNames.stream()
        .distinct()
        .map(
            className ->
                HelperClassDefinition.create(className, helpersSource, InjectionMode.CLASS_ONLY))
        .collect(toList());
```

threads.body: [General] Making `getOrNull` abstract while turning `getOrDefault` into a default method is source- and binary-incompatible for existing `Trie` implementations. Classes compiled against the current interface implement only `getOrDefault`, so invoking `getOrNull` with the new interface can fail with `AbstractMethodError`. Since this PR only needs to enable NullAway, please retain the existing abstract/default method layout, using a narrowly scoped NullAway suppression for the intentional null sentinel, and keep the implementation in `TrieImpl`.

replies.body: Good catch — I updated this in the refreshed branch to preserve the original interface layout for compatibility. `Trie.getOrNull(...)` is default again, `Trie.getOrDefault(...)` stays abstract, and the null-sentinel handling remains in `TrieImpl`. For NullAway I used a narrowly scoped suppression on the default `getOrNull(...)` implementation, which is the only place intentionally passing `null` as the no-match sentinel.
Removed that extra null-tightening. `InstrumentationModuleInstaller` now just stores the constructor argument as-is again.
